newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen small up, aluminium down.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen small up, aluminium down.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks will probably post a small increase of about 2,000-3,000 tonnes while the amount of copper trickling into Singapore appears to have dried up, traders said on Friday.
Aluminium stocks, however, are likely to dip by between 500-1,000 tonnes when the LME report is released later on Friday at 0900 GMT, the traders said.
"Copper should be a small up while aluminium will be a small down," a trader for a Japanese metal trading company said.
The amount of copper being shipped to the LME warehouse in the city-state has slowed substantially, dealers said.
"I've not heard of any material that has come in lately," a dealer for a European metal trading firm firm said.
The LME warehouse in Singapore contained 23,750 tonnes of copper on Tuesday, up 2,325 tonnes from last Friday's report. Traders estimate about 10,000 tonnes remain off-warrant here.
"Some of the material should go on warrant shortly," one trader said.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers in Singapore at around US$2,162/67 a tonne at 0230 GMT, little changed from the late trade in London on Thursday of $2,162/65 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were quoted by dealers at 0230 GMT at about $1,554/57 a tonne, also practically unchanged from the late trade in London yesterday of $1,552/54 a tonne.
